safety_argument.cited: MULTI_ORG_TENANT_SCOPE_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json REQUEST_REVALIDATION.preserved_mechanism: 'The existing per-request mechanism at db/identity-context.ts withDatabaseIdentityContext is genuine revalidation today and is PRESERVED (PI-4, PI-9). S3 changes WHAT is revalidated (membership in the selected organization) rather than WHETHER revalidation happens.'
safety_argument.consequence: Per-request revalidation against live database state ALREADY happens at START_HEAD. It currently revalidates the pick-first membership (SI-2, lib/auth/database-context.ts:210/:219). Shipping S2 does not remove, weaken, bypass or race that mechanism, because S2 adds a cookie that NOTHING reads for authorization.
safety_argument.therefore: The tenant-isolation posture after S2-alone is byte-for-byte the posture before S2-alone. S2 alone cannot be a security regression because it changes no authorization input.
safety_argument.the_condition_that_makes_this_true: The carrier must be INERT. See S2.INERTNESS_RULE. If an implementing mission wires the carrier into principal construction, role resolution, RLS, a GUC or any capability check, this safety argument is VOID and that mission has silently performed S3 without its lineage.

trust_model_objection_answered.objection: SELECTED_ORG_CARRIER.trust_model says a forged or stale cookie 'must produce a refusal, never data'. Does shipping the cookie without S3 violate that?
trust_model_objection_answered.answer: No. That clause governs what must happen when the carrier is CONSUMED as a scope. Under INERTNESS the carrier is never consumed as a scope, so there is no request in which a forged cookie could yield data: the pre-existing revalidation decides scope exactly as it does today and never consults the cookie. The obligation attaches to S3, which is where consumption begins, and it is carried forward unchanged as an S3 precondition.
trust_model_objection_answered.residual_risk_stated_plainly: The honest residual is not a data-exposure risk but a SEQUENCING risk - a later mission may consume the carrier without noticing that revalidation was never retargeted. Control NS2-4 exists to fail loudly in exactly that case.

compiler_warning_adjudicated.verdict: WARNING UPHELD, AND STRONGER THAN STATED.
compiler_warning_adjudicated.why_a_naive_index_is_wrong: A partial unique index of the shape UNIQUE(founded_by) WHERE founded_by IS NOT NULL binds the COLUMN globally. FOUNDER_CARDINALITY.explicitly_not_implied forbids exactly that: the cardinality 'binds the SELF-SERVICE FOUNDING ACT, not the founded_by column globally', and explicitly permits additional organizations whose founded_by names the same subject through a NON-self-service path. Under the naive index, a platform-admin-created organization that honestly records its deterministic provenance would CONSUME the subject's one self-service slot and permanently block their own founding - a correctness failure produced by recording the truth.

REQUIRED_RESOLUTION.rule: The implementing mission MUST introduce a DURABLE SELF-SERVICE PROVENANCE DISCRIMINATOR that the cardinality predicate can reference, and MUST enforce the cardinality at the DATABASE boundary.
REQUIRED_RESOLUTION.why_a_discriminator_is_unavoidable: MEASURED. organizations carries no provenance/kind/origin column at START_HEAD (inspected db/schema.ts:17-40 and the full table definition). Without one there is no predicate that can distinguish a self-service founding from a platform-admin founding, so no partial index can express MO-01 correctly. The discriminator is therefore not a design preference; it is the minimum information the constraint needs to exist.
REQUIRED_RESOLUTION.shape: The exact discriminator (for example a founding-provenance enum column on organizations, defaulting to the honest 'unknown' for historical rows) is DEFERRED to the implementing mission and MUST be chosen against the live schema. It MUST admit at least: self-service founding, non-self-service founding, and UNKNOWN.
hard_constraints: MUST NOT retroactively constrain historical rows whose founded_by is NULL under MO-11. A backfill that leaves NULLs and a cardinality rule that rejects NULLs must coexist - carried forward verbatim from TARGET_SCHEMA.founder_cardinality_carrier.hard_constraint.

MUST NOT be enforced only in application code. SELF_SERVICE_BOOTSTRAP.serialization_replacement.prohibited establishes the repository rule that replacing a database uniqueness guarantee with an application read-then-write check is 'a downgrade disguised as a refactor'. The same rule binds here.
MUST NOT make the discriminator readable by any authorization path. founded_by and its provenance discriminator are traceability only (PI-3).
MUST NOT default historical rows to the self-service value. Unknown provenance is UNKNOWN.
REQUIRED_RESOLUTION.failure_behavior: A second self-service founding attempt by the same subject MUST fail closed with TENANCY_FOUNDER_CARDINALITY_EXCEEDED, never silently succeed and never silently reuse the existing organization.

S1_BACKFILL.unknown_disposition: NULL. Not a sentinel user, not a placeholder uuid, not the platform account, not the first admin.

A backfill whose outcome cannot be reproduced is not deterministic and does not satisfy MO-11.
S1_BACKFILL.irreversibility: A wrong attribution is unrecoverable, because a wrong value becomes indistinguishable from a right one. This asymmetry is why the rule is conservative rather than best-effort.

S2_SESSION_CARRIER.decision: A session cookie carrying the selected organization identity. Exactly one selected organization is the tenant request scope at a time.

S2_SESSION_CARRIER.explicit_selection_required: A request with no selected organization is NOT silently defaulted to a membership. Where the subject has exactly one selectable membership the application MAY present it, but MUST make an EXPLICIT selection by writing the carrier, never by inferring scope at request time. Multi-membership: the subject is asked. No pick-first, no most-recent, no alphabetical default.

path_scope.obligation: The implementing mission MUST choose the cookie Path against the live route tree so the carrier is not sent to routes with no business receiving it, and MUST record the measured route set that justified the choice.
path_scope.measured_input: At START_HEAD the authenticated route group app/(authenticated)/app/ contains exactly ONE route - onboarding - while the main product surface lives under app/app/. The Path choice must be made against that real split and not assumed to be '/'.

prohibited_carriers: localStorage or sessionStorage - not HttpOnly, readable by any script on the origin
a URL path segment or query parameter - leaks tenant scope into logs, referrers and shared links
a request header set by client-side code - trivially forgeable, invisible to cookie policy
a persisted database column on users - would survive the session and violate SESSION_SCOPE
S2_COOKIE_CONTRACT.trust_model: THE CARRIER IS AN ASSERTION, NEVER A GRANT. Hard to forge is not the same as validated. This is carried into S3 as a precondition and is NOT discharged by S2.

INERTNESS_RULE.status: THE LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINT OF THIS BATCH. It is what makes S3's exclusion safe AND what makes S1/S2 parallel-safe. If it is violated, both properties fail together.
INERTNESS_RULE.rule: In this batch the carrier is WRITTEN, READ BACK and CLEARED, and is consumed by NOTHING that participates in an authorization decision.
prohibited_in_this_batch: reading the carrier in db/identity-context.ts (CP-5) or in any GUC assignment
reading the carrier in lib/auth/database-context.ts, including loadRequestPrincipal and loadActiveMembershipWithinContext (:210, the SI-2 site whose .limit(1) sits at :219)
reading the carrier in lib/auth/session.ts, lib/auth/permissions.ts or lib/auth/roles.ts
using the carrier in any RLS predicate, policy, capability check, role resolution or entitlement evaluation
using the carrier to select, filter or scope any tenant row
INERTNESS_RULE.consequence_if_violated: The mission has silently performed S3 without S3's lineage, without REQUEST_REVALIDATION, and without the N-1/N-2 controls that exist to catch precisely that. Control NS2-4 is the detector and is mandatory.
INERTNESS_RULE.what_S2_may_legitimately_do: Write the carrier from an explicit selection action; read it back to render which organization is selected; clear it. Nothing else.

S2_EXACT_PATHS.semantics: CEILING, not mandate. Subset permitted; superset fails closed.
S2_EXACT_PATHS.protected_grant_rationale: MEASURED. No path S2 needs matches any of the seven DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS entries. S2 touches no db/**, no docs/ops/fib/**, no docs/ops/pc01b/** and no docs/ops/im01b/**. S2 therefore requires NO protected grant of any kind - a direct consequence of the carrier being a session cookie rather than a database column.
S2_EXACT_PATHS.new_files_note: All five are new at START_HEAD. lib/auth/selected-organization.ts is the substantive deliverable and is deliberately a NEW module rather than an addition to lib/auth/session.ts or lib/auth/database-context.ts: those are S3 surfaces, and keeping the carrier in its own module is what makes the INERTNESS_RULE mechanically checkable by import-graph inspection rather than by reading prose.
explicitly_NOT_authorized: db/schema.ts - S2 adds no column. SESSION_SCOPE forbids persisting the selection.
db/identity-context.ts (CP-5), lib/auth/database-context.ts, lib/auth/session.ts - INERTNESS_RULE and S3 ownership.
app/(authenticated)/app/onboarding/actions.ts - owned exclusively by S1 this batch. See PARALLELISM.the_one_real_collision.
lib/auth/identity.ts - the Supabase auth cookie is a different carrier with a different lifetime.

the_one_real_collision.finding: The compiler's parallel-safety report is CORRECT but INCOMPLETE, and the gap it leaves is not visible from the DAG. A natural S2 implementation auto-selects the newly founded organization immediately after self-service founding. That write would land in app/(authenticated)/app/onboarding/actions.ts - the single file S1 must also edit to write founded_by. Under concurrent lanes that is a genuine shared writer producing a silent textual merge on the exact transaction S1 is changing.
the_one_real_collision.resolution: app/(authenticated)/app/onboarding/actions.ts is assigned EXCLUSIVELY to S1 for this batch. S2 MUST NOT write the carrier there.
the_one_real_collision.why_this_costs_nothing: The resolution is not a compromise forced by scheduling - it is what SESSION_SCOPE.no_selection_behavior already mandates. That clause requires selection to be made by an EXPLICIT selection act writing the carrier, and forbids inferring a scope, including in the single-membership case. Auto-selecting inside the founding transaction is precisely the inference it forbids. The disjointness constraint and the product doctrine agree, so no functionality is deferred by honouring it.
the_one_real_collision.post_founding_behavior: After self-service founding the subject has NO selection until they make one explicitly. This is correct by MO-04 and is asserted by control NS2-5.

PARALLELISM.recommended_execution: TWO INDEPENDENT LANES, concurrent. S1 on codex/multiorg-s1-founder-traceability-r1; S2 on codex/multiorg-s2-selected-org-carrier-r1. Each opens its own prestate/scope/poststate gates against its own allowlist. Neither may pass the other's paths to --allow.
PARALLELISM.if_the_lanes_are_run_serially_instead: Permitted and harmless. Order is immaterial because the sets are disjoint and neither node depends on the other.

Only controls that do not exist there are added, and every addition is justified by the S2-alone gap measured in WHY_THIS_ARTIFACT_IS_REQUIRED.GAP_3.
TEST_CONTRACT.why_no_second_manifest: The existing manifest is node_or_batch='batch' and already covers S1 and S2 as members of S1..S8. INHERITED_BINDING.note_on_N1_and_N2: N-1 and N-2 are the controls that would catch carrier misuse, and both are S3-tagged. They are NOT inherited because S3 is not implemented here and a control asserting behavior no code implements is vacuous. NS2-4 replaces them for this batch by asserting the STRONGER property that no consumption exists at all.

ADDED_S1_CONTROLS.S1-1: SELF_SERVICE_PROVENANCE DISCRIMINATOR EXISTS. organizations carries a durable provenance discriminator, and it admits at least self-service, non-self-service and UNKNOWN. Fails if the implementation relies on founded_by alone.
ADDED_S1_CONTROLS.S1-2: PLATFORM-CREATED ORGANIZATION DOES NOT CONSUME THE SLOT. A subject who is recorded as the deterministic provenance of a NON-self-service organization may still self-service-found exactly one organization. THIS IS THE CONTROL THE NAIVE PARTIAL INDEX FAILS, and it is the reason the discriminator is mandatory.
ADDED_S1_CONTROLS.S1-3: AMBIGUOUS BACKFILL RESOLVES TO NULL. An organization with zero, or with more than one, qualifying 'organization.created' audit row is left NULL. Never a first pick, never an earliest pick.
ADDED_S1_CONTROLS.S1-4: CARDINALITY IS ENFORCED AT THE DATABASE BOUNDARY, asserted against live database metadata rather than against db/schema.ts, so a silently lost declaration (CP-2) fails rather than passes.
ADDED_S1_CONTROLS.S1-5: NULLS COEXIST WITH THE CARDINALITY RULE. Multiple historical organizations with founded_by NULL are accepted simultaneously; the constraint does not collapse them.
ADDED_S1_CONTROLS.S1-6: FOUNDED_BY IS WRITTEN IN THE FOUNDING TRANSACTION. A successful self-service founding yields founded_by = the founder and the self-service provenance value, committed atomically with the organization row - never as a follow-up write that can be lost.

ADDED_S2_CONTROLS.NS2-1: COOKIE ATTRIBUTES ARE EXACT. The carrier is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, with NO Max-Age and NO Expires. Each attribute asserted individually - a single combined assertion can pass while one attribute is missing.
ADDED_S2_CONTROLS.NS2-2: SESSION-ONLY IN FACT. The selection does not survive a new session, and no users column, preference row or other persistent store holds it.
ADDED_S2_CONTROLS.NS2-3: CARRIER TAMPERING IS INERT AND NON-FATAL. A carrier naming an unknown organization id, a malformed id, an organization the subject is not a member of, a suspended organization, a stale/removed-membership organization, or a CommercialAccount id supplied where an organization id is expected, MUST NOT yield that organization's data and MUST NOT crash the request. Under INERTNESS the request resolves exactly as it does today, because scope never consults the carrier. Cookie deletion and session expiry yield NO selection, never a default.
ADDED_S2_CONTROLS.NS2-4: INERTNESS DETECTOR - THE MANDATORY CONTROL OF THIS BATCH. No authorization surface imports or reads the carrier. Asserted mechanically over the import graph and source of db/identity-context.ts, lib/auth/database-context.ts, lib/auth/session.ts, lib/auth/permissions.ts and lib/auth/roles.ts. Fails if any of them references lib/auth/selected-organization.ts or the carrier's cookie name. This control is what converts the S3-exclusion safety argument from prose into a machine-checked property, and it MUST be retired deliberately by S3 rather than deleted quietly.
ADDED_S2_CONTROLS.NS2-5: NO INFERRED SELECTION. A subject with exactly one selectable membership has NO carrier until an explicit selection act writes one, and a subject who has just self-service-founded an organization likewise has no carrier. Asserts MO-04 and simultaneously proves the S1/S2 collision resolution held.
ADDED_S2_CONTROLS.NS2-6: SUPERADMIN IS NOT EXEMPT FROM SELECTION. A platform super_admin obtains no implicit tenant scope from the absence of a carrier and no bypass from its presence. Scoped to S2's inert surface only; the full SUPERADMIN_BOUNDARY obligation (N-3) remains S5's.

MUTATION_CONTROLS.rule: Each mutation must be applied to a WORKING tree and must produce a FAILING control. A mutation harness must additionally assert that the file actually changed on disk, so a no-op edit cannot masquerade as a passing control.
MUTATION_CONTROLS.MS1-1: Guarantee: the cardinality carrier discriminates self-service provenance. Mutation: widen the partial index predicate to `WHERE founded_by IS NOT NULL`, dropping the provenance conjunct. Expected: S1-2 FAILS. This is the exact naive-index defect the compiler warned about; a batch whose controls survive this mutation has not implemented MO-01.
MUTATION_CONTROLS.MS1-2: Guarantee: the MO-11 backfill prohibition (binds M-5). Mutation: add `invited_by IS NULL` as a backfill predicate. Expected: S1-3 and P-2 FAIL.
MUTATION_CONTROLS.MS1-3: Guarantee: founded_by grants nothing, PI-3 (binds M-6). Mutation: add founded_by as a disjunct to any authorization predicate. Expected: N-9 FAILS.
MUTATION_CONTROLS.MS1-4: Guarantee: unknown provenance stays NULL. Mutation: default the provenance discriminator to the self-service value for historical rows. Expected: S1-3 and S1-5 FAIL.
MUTATION_CONTROLS.MS2-1: Guarantee: the carrier dies with the session. Mutation: add a Max-Age to the cookie. Expected: NS2-1 and NS2-2 FAIL.
MUTATION_CONTROLS.MS2-2: Guarantee: the carrier is HttpOnly. Mutation: set HttpOnly false. Expected: NS2-1 FAILS.
MUTATION_CONTROLS.MS2-3: Guarantee: INERTNESS. Mutation: read the carrier inside loadActiveMembershipWithinContext and use it to qualify the membership lookup. Expected: NS2-4 FAILS. NOTE - this mutation makes the system arguably MORE correct in product terms; the control must still fail, because the change is S3 and requires S3's lineage and revalidation contract. A control that passes here is not a control.
MUTATION_CONTROLS.MS2-4: Guarantee: explicit selection only. Mutation: auto-select the sole membership at request time when no carrier is present. Expected: NS2-5 FAILS.

REAL_PG_FUTURE_CONTROLS.rule: MANDATORY for S1 because its guarantees are database semantics. A unit test over Drizzle types cannot prove a partial unique index exists or that a constraint rejects a write.
REAL_PG_FUTURE_CONTROLS.PG-S1-1: The partial unique carrier REJECTS a second self-service founding by the same subject with the correct failure, under a real INSERT.
REAL_PG_FUTURE_CONTROLS.PG-S1-2: The same carrier ACCEPTS a non-self-service organization recording the same subject as provenance. PG-S1-1 and PG-S1-2 together are the discriminator proof; either alone is passable by a wrong implementation.
REAL_PG_FUTURE_CONTROLS.PG-S1-3: The backfill's attributed / left-NULL counts are recomputable from the same inputs and match the recorded evidence exactly.
REAL_PG_FUTURE_CONTROLS.PG-S1-4: ON DELETE RESTRICT is enforced: deleting a users row referenced by organizations.founded_by is refused by the database, not by application code.
REAL_PG_FUTURE_CONTROLS.PG-S1-5: CONCURRENT BOOTSTRAP. Two simultaneous self-service founding attempts by the SAME subject yield exactly one organization and one refusal. Must be run under real concurrency, since a read-then-write check passes serially and fails only here.
REAL_PG_FUTURE_CONTROLS.S2_real_pg: NOT REQUIRED. Measured: S2 introduces no database object, no column, no policy and no GUC. Stating this affirmatively because REAL_PG_CONTRACT is mandatory for the batch as a whole and a reader could otherwise assume S2 inherits it. If an implementing mission finds itself needing a PG probe for S2, that is evidence the INERTNESS_RULE has been broken.
